page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores using Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz, configured with 1 thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic acceleration. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. This instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average performance in core system metrics alongside lower throughput in specialized computational workloads. Stress-ng tests place both single-core (1812.79) and multi-core (7217.84) processing in the middle 50% percentile, accompanied by mid-tier uncached memory bandwidth of 47.64 GB/sec read and 28.32 GB/sec write. In contrast, Geekbench single-core (1062.0) and multi-core (3517.0) ratings fall into the lower quartile, as do targeted operations like Clang compilation (4864.0) and ray tracing (4216.0). Small model (135M) LLM text processing achieves 162.41 tokens/sec for prompts and 34.59 tokens/sec for generation, placing it in the bottom 10% tier.

Cost efficiency for the t2a-standard-4 is defined by its Arm-native density and dedicated core allocation. By avoiding simultaneous multithreading, it delivers stable per-vCPU throughput without resource contention, making it an efficient deployment target for Linux-based microservices, containerized workloads, CI/CD pipelines, and application backends designed for arm64 execution. Workloads requiring heavy floating-point calculation, advanced vector instructions (AVX/AMX), or integrated high-speed local disk storage will face bottlenecks due to missing hardware extensions and reliance on remote block devices.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-4 is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by a 4-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz with 1 thread per core. It is configured with 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, zero GPUs, and no integrated local storage. In benchmark assessments, it achieves mid-range scores in stress-ng single-core (1812.79) and multi-core (7217.84) execution, along with stable uncached memory throughput. However, instruction sets lack x86 vector extensions like AVX-512, contributing to lower quartile scores in Geekbench multi-core (3517.0) and cryptographic tests. Offering cost-effective dedicated compute without hyperthreading contention, t2a-standard-4 is well structured for arm-native container workloads, web serving, CI/CD runners, and general microservices.
